description: Kill the pricing N+1 and reuse eager-loaded relations (F-7, P-1, P-2, P-3). PricingService::calculate() calls AttributeOption::find() per option then optionPrices()->first() per option. ConfiguratorService::evaluate() eager-loads rules/BOM/compatibility relations but RuleEngineService, BomGeneratorService, and CompatibilityService re-query them, discarding the eager load. Batch-load options and have the services consume the already-loaded relations. Depends on FEAT-001 (ConditionEvaluator in those services) and should land after FEAT-002/003/004 so the final service shapes are stable (it edits the same services).
steps: PricingService::calculate(): gather all numeric option ids from $selections first, then issue ONE query AttributeOption::with('optionPrices')->whereIn('id', $ids)->get()->keyBy('id'); resolve each option's price_list adjustment from the in-memory optionPrices collection (filter by price_list_id in PHP), falling back to option->price_adjustment. Remove the per-option find() and per-option optionPrices()->where()->first(). Preserve the cents math from FEAT-002 and the return shape.

Make RuleEngineService::evaluate(), BomGeneratorService::generate(), and CompatibilityService::getDisabledOptions() CONSUME the relations already loaded on the Product by ConfiguratorService::evaluate() (read $product->configurationRules, $product->bomRules, $product->compatibilityRules as loaded collections) instead of calling $product->xxxRules()->with(...)->get(). Because the relation methods bake in is_active (and ordering), ensure ConfiguratorService's ->load([...]) uses those same constrained relations so a single load satisfies all consumers and the is_active/sort_order guarantees are preserved.

Adjust the eager-load tree in ConfiguratorService::evaluate() so one load() satisfies rules (conditions.attribute, actions), BOM (conditions.attribute, items.component.category — note BomGeneratorService needs items.component.category for the 'type' field), compatibility (attribute, option, targetAttribute, targetOption, and the target attribute's options for FEAT-004's complement), part number pattern, and productAttributes.attribute.options. Keep services working when a relation is already loaded (guard with relationLoaded or load-if-missing, but default path must not re-query when evaluate() provided it).

Add tests/Feature/ConfiguratorPerformanceTest.php (Pest): enable Model::preventLazyLoading() (or use DB::listen to count queries) for the test; build a product graph with multiple attributes/options/rules; assert ConfiguratorService::evaluate() triggers NO lazy loading and a bounded total query count (<= a documented constant). Separately assert PricingService::calculate() issues a single options query whether 1 or many options are selected (parametrize and compare counts). Run Pint and targeted tests, then the full suite.
acceptance_criteria: PricingService::calculate() issues exactly one query to load the selected AttributeOptions (with optionPrices) regardless of option count; no per-option find()/first() remains.
RuleEngineService, BomGeneratorService, and CompatibilityService read the eager-loaded relations from the Product instead of re-querying on the default evaluate() path.
ConfiguratorService::evaluate() runs with no lazy-loading violations and a bounded query count (ConfiguratorPerformanceTest passes with preventLazyLoading).
Phase 1 is_active / sort_order filtering on rules/BOM/compatibility is preserved.
BomParity, RuleEngineActions, CompatibilityRules, and Money tests still pass; full suite green.
findings:
DONE. Full suite green: 41 passed (97 assertions) = 39 prior + ConfiguratorPerformanceTest 2. Regression set (BomParity, RuleEngineActions, CompatibilityRules, MoneyHandling) = 13 passed, unchanged. Pint clean.

=== PricingService::calculate() N+1 removed ===
Added private collectOptionIds(array $selections): list<int> that flattens selections into a de-duplicated, selection-ordered list of numeric option ids. calculate() now issues ONE query: AttributeOption::query()->with('optionPrices')->whereIn('id', $ids)->get()->keyBy('id'). Per option it reads the in-memory optionPrices collection via ->firstWhere('price_list_id', $priceList->id)?->price_adjustment ?? $option->price_adjustment (filter in PHP, no per-option optionPrices()->where()->first()). The per-option AttributeOption::find() is gone. Cents math (FEAT-002) and return shape (base_price, option_adjustments[].adjustment, options_total, subtotal, discount=0, total, currency) unchanged. ConfiguratorPerformanceTest asserts exactly 1 'attribute_options' query whether 1 or 3 options are selected.

=== Services consume ConfiguratorService's eager load ===
ConfiguratorService::evaluate() now calls $product->loadMissing([...]) (was ->load, which discarded any caller-provided graph). Loading THROUGH the Product relation methods (configurationRules/bomRules/compatibilityRules/partNumberPattern) preserves Phase 1 is_active + ordering (priority / sort_order).
RuleEngineService::evaluate(): reads $product->configurationRules (loaded collection) after a loadMissing(['configurationRules.conditions.attribute','configurationRules.actions']) guard for standalone use; removed the ->configurationRules()->with(...)->get() re-query. applyDisableOption() keeps its single AttributeOption::find(target_id) on the disable_option action path only (not an N+1 over selections; a fresh query, not lazy loading).
BomGeneratorService::generate(): reads $product->bomRules (loaded collection) after a loadMissing(['bomRules.conditions.attribute','bomRules.items.component.category']) guard; removed the ->bomRules()->with(...)->where('is_active',true)->orderBy('sort_order')->get() re-query (is_active + sort_order still come from the bomRules relation definition).
CompatibilityService::getDisabledOptions(): reads $product->compatibilityRules (loaded collection) after a loadMissing of attribute/option/targetAttribute.options/targetOption; the compatible-complement reads $rule->targetAttribute->options (eager-loaded) and filters is_active in PHP, replacing the per-target AttributeOption::query()->where('attribute_id',..)->where('is_active',true)->pluck('id'). Behavior identical (Attribute::options() does not filter is_active, so the PHP is_active guard matches the old SQL filter).
Guard pattern: every consumer uses loadMissing so the default evaluate() path does NOT re-query (relation already present), while standalone service use still works (load-if-missing through the constrained relation).

=== FINAL eager-load tree (ConfiguratorService::evaluate loadMissing) ===
productAttributes.attribute.options
configurationRules.conditions.attribute
configurationRules.actions
bomRules.conditions.attribute
bomRules.items.component.category
compatibilityRules.attribute
compatibilityRules.option
compatibilityRules.targetAttribute.options
compatibilityRules.targetOption
partNumberPattern

=== Bounded query-count constant ===
tests/Feature/ConfiguratorPerformanceTest.php defines const CONFIGURATOR_MAX_QUERIES = 25. The test enables Model::preventLazyLoading(true) around evaluate() (no lazy-load violation thrown) and asserts total DB::listen query count <= 25 for a graph of 3 attributes x3 options, 2 config rules (condition+action each), 2 BOM rules (1 item each), 1 compatibility rule. Separately asserts PricingService::calculate() issues exactly ONE 'attribute_options' query for both 1 and 3 selections.

=== Preserved ===
is_active / sort_order / priority filtering on rules/BOM/compatibility (via the Product relation definitions, now the single load source). FEAT-002 cents math, FEAT-003 rule actions + visibility, FEAT-004 symmetric incompatible + compatible complement behavior all unchanged (regression tests green).
